newsitem.title: USA: Floodgates open as U.S. corporate debt issues flow.
newsitem.headline: Floodgates open as U.S. corporate debt issues flow.

text.p: The floodgates have opened and corporate debt issues continue to pour in as issuers capitalize on falling interest rates, dealers said.
On Wednesday about $3.0 billion in new straight corporate debt was priced in the primary market, with over $2.0 billion coming from the high-grade sector alone, dealers said.
More of the same is expected on Thursday, as another $1.5 billion in investment grade debt is slated to come to market, players said.
"There's lots of supply out there and spreads are staying firm right now," said one high-grade syndicate official.
"This would indicate a couple of things, either deals are moving well and/or dealers are taking things down," he added.
However, most syndicate players agreed that the recent flood of debt offerings have met with very good demand by investors.
A rally in the U.S. Treasury market has seen the yield on the benchmark 30-year bond drop from 6.71 percent close on July 2, to 6.32 percent, where it is currently trading.
Meanwhile, Harcourt General Inc is expected to issue its $500 million three-part debt offering consisting of 10-year, 30-year and 100-year issues, dealers said.

Mirage Resorts Inc is expected to bring a two-part debt offering which is expected to include $150 million in 10-year debt and $100 million in 20-year debt via lead underwriter Credit Suisse First Boston.
Unofficial price talk on the 10-year issue is seen at 85 basis points over Treasuries and 100 basis points over on the 20-year, dealers said.
Mirage Resorts, formerly Golden Nugget, owns two Las Vegas casino hotels, a casino in Laughlin Nevada and property in the Atlantic City marina area.
Omega Health is slated to bring a $100 million 10-year debt offering via JP Morgan Securities, players said.
Maxsaver Finance is also rumored to bring a $150 million 10-year debt offering via Goldman Sachs & Co, players said.
Among other high-grade issuers, Florida Windstorm Association is planning a $500 million two-part 144a debt offering via Chase Securities.
The deal is expected to include $250 million in five-years and $250 million in 10-year debt, sources said.
